BEEP:
Plays a SID beep.

BEEP [duration]

Duration is in milliseconds. The
default value when omitted is 200 ms.
CHKDSK:
Checks a disk and returns a status
report.

CHKDSK [drive:] [/V | /C]

  /V  Checks and fixes all formatted
      1581 subpartitions and all CMD
      DOS partitions, including native
      subdirectories.
  /C  Compacts the cartridge file system
      journal.

CMD /V reports validation completion;
its allocation report is not disk-wide.
Omit drive to check the current disk.
COPY:
Copies a file to another location, or
combines files on the same disk.

COPY source [destination] [/P]
COPY source1+source2[+...] destination
COPY CON filename [/O]
COPY filename PRN

  source
       File(s) to copy.
  destination
       Specifies the path and/or file
       name for the new file(s).
  /P   Suppresses confirmation prompt to
       prompt to overwrite an existing
       file.
  /-P  Causes confirmation prompt to
       overwrite an existing file, even
       when suppressed with COPYCMD.
DEL:
Deletes one or more files.

DEL [drive:][path]filename [/P]
DELETE [drive:][path]filename [/P]
ERASE [drive:][path]filename [/P]

  /P   Suppresses confirmation prompt
       before deleting a file.
  /-P  Causes confirmation prompt before
       deleting a file, even when
       suppressed with DELCMD.
DIR:
Displays a list of files on a disk.

DIR [drive:][path][pattern] [/A] [/B]
    [/C] [/D] [/L] [/N] [/O] [/S] [/T]
    [/W]

  /A     Displays files with specified
         attributes.
           D  Directories
           L  Locked files
  /B     Uses bare format (names only).
  /C     Shows compact listing including
         timestamps.
  /D     Displays timestamps instead of
         file sizes.
  /L     Uses lower-case.
  /N     Displays native FAT file names
         (Ultimate).
  /O     Lists files in sorted order
  order   N  By name (alphabetic)
          T  By type (alphabetic)
          S  By size (smallest first)
          -  Prefix to reverse
  /S     Displays files in directory
         and all subdirectories.
  /T     Lists files of given type.
  type    D  DEL    I  Disk images
          P  PRG    R  REL
          S  SEQ    U  USR
  /W     Uses wide list format.
DISKCOPY:
Copies the contents of one disk to
another.

DISKCOPY source: destination:
  source:       Drive to copy from.
  destination:  Drive to copy to.

Note: source and destination drive must
have matching 1541/1571/1581 formats.
On CMD devices, copies the selected
emulation partition only.
ECHO:
Displays messages, or turns command-
echoing on or off.

  ECHO [ON | OFF]
  ECHO [message]

Type ECHO without parameters to display
the current echo setting. ECHO. (no
space) will insert a blank line.
EDIT:
Edits one screen of text.

EDIT [drive:][path][filename]
BASIC:
Starts the C64 BASIC environment.

In BASIC, type SHELL to return.
FORMAT:
Formats a disk.

FORMAT drive: [/V:label] [/I:id]
              [/F:format]

  /V:label   Specifies the volume label.
  /I:id      Specifies the disk ID.
  /Q         Performs a quick format.
  /F:format  Specifies a CMD-FD format
             type: 81, DD8, HD8, ED8,
             DDN, HDN, EDN, S8 or SW.
HELP:
Displays help on MCS-DOS commands.

  HELP [command]

[command]
  Displays help on that command.

COMMAND /? also displays help. If no
command is specified, a list of valid
commands is displayed.
LABEL:
Creates, changes, or deletes the volume
label of a disk.

LABEL [drive:] [label]
MEM:
Displays the amount of used and free
memory in your system.

MEM
MOVE:
Moves a file to another location, or
renames a directory within its parent.

MOVE source destination [/P]

  /P   Suppresses confirmation prompt to
       prompt to overwrite an existing
       file.
  /-P  Causes confirmation prompt to
       overwrite an existing file, even
       when suppressed with COPYCMD.
PAUSE:
Suspends processing of a batch program
and waits for a key to resume.

PAUSE [message]
PRINT:
Sends the contents of a file to a
printer.

PRINT filename [PRN|LPT1|LPT2|4:|5:]

Omit the printer to use PRN. Set PRN in
CONFIG.SYS. LPT1 and LPT2 select IEC
devices 4 and 5.
REM:
Records comments in a batch file.

REM [comment]
REN:
Changes the name of a file or directory.

REN [drive:][path]filename1
    [drive:][path]filename2
RENAME [drive:][path]filename1
       [drive:][path]filename2
RUN:
Executes a program.

RUN [drive:][path]filename [/A address]

  /A  Load at and jump to at the decimal
      address.
TYPE:
Displays the contents of a file.

TYPE [drive:][path]filename
     [/H[:n] | /T[:n] [/C]] [/HEX]

  /H:n  Shows first n lines of file.
  /T:n  Shows last n lines of file.
  /C    Specifies a number of bytes
        instead of lines.
  /HEX  Shows a hex view.

n defaults to 10 lines or bytes if not
specified.
VOL:
Displays the volume label (disk name)
and disk ID, if they exist.
VER:
Displays the MCS-DOS version and
copyright information.

VER
DISKID:
Changes the drive's two-character ID.

DISKID [drive:] [id]

ID must be two letters or digits. Omit
the ID to be prompted.
SET:
Displays, sets, or removes  environment
variables.

SET [variable=[string]]
SET /ENV
  variable  Specifies the environment
            variable name.
  string    Specifies a series of
            characters to assign to the
            variable.
  /ENV      Displays environment usage
            statistics.

Type SET without parameters to display
the current environment variables.

Variable names can be up to 8 characters
long, and values up to 32 characters.
ATTRIB:
Displays or changes file attributes

ATTRIB [+L | -L]
       [[drive:][path]filename]

  +   Sets an attribute.
  -   Clears an attribute.
  L   File lock attribute.
SYSINFO:
Provides technical information about
your computer.

SYSINFO
FIND:
Searches for a text string in a file.

FIND [/V] [/C] [/N] [/I] "string"
     [drive:][path]filename

 /V  Displays all lines NOT containing
     the specified string.
 /C  Displays only the count of lines
     containing the string.
 /N  Displays line numbers with the
     displayed lines
 /I  Ignores the case of characters
     when searching for the string
 "string"
     Specifies the text string to find.
 [drive:]filename
     Specifies a file to search.
DISKINIT:
Resets disk drive state and forces a
reread of the directory.
TAPECOPY:
Loads and transfers one or more files
from tape to disk.

TAPECOPY [filename] [destination]

  filename  The name of the file to seek
            and load.
  destination  Target drive or directory.
KEY:
Binds command text to function keys.

KEY [/Fn[:command] ...] [/CLEAR[:n]]

  /Fn:command
    Binds a command to a function key.
    n is 1 to 7.
  /Fn
    Displays the current binding for
    the specified function key.
  /CLEAR:n
    Clears the binding for one function
    key.
  /CLEAR
    Clears all bindings.

Type KEY without parameters to display
all current bindings.
CD:
Changes or displays the current
directory or partition.

CD [drive:][path] [/D]
CHDIR [drive:][path] [/D]

  /D  Changes drive in addition to
      changing directory on that drive.
MD:
Creates a directory or partition.

MD [drive:][path] [/SIZE:n]
MKDIR [drive:][path] [/SIZE:n]

  /SIZE:n  Specifies the partition size
           for 1581 drives (minimum 120
           sectors, multiple of 40).
RD:
Removes a directory or partition.

RD [drive:][path] [/S [/P]]
RMDIR [drive:][path]

  /S   Removes all directories and files
       in the specified directory as
       well. Not supported on CMD native
       directories.
  /P   Suppresses confirmation prompt
       before removing a directory with
       /S.
  /-P  Causes confirmation prompt before
       removing a directory, even when
       suppressed with DELCMD.
MOUNT:
Mounts a disk image.

MOUNT image [drive:]

This command is only supported on SD2IEC
or Ultimate devices.

Ultimate accepts quoted native long file
names, including spaces and commas.
Parent directories use MCS-DOS paths.
UNMOUNT:
Unmount a disk image.

UNMOUNT [drive:]

This command is only supported on SD2IEC
or Ultimate devices.
MAKEDISK:
Creates a blank disk image.

MAKEDISK [drive:][path]filename
         [/V:label] [/I:id]

  /V:label  Specifies the volume label.
  /I:id     Specifies the disk ID.
DATE:
Displays or sets the date.

DATE [drive:] [/T | date] [/D]

  /D  Shows the selected clock device.
  /T  Shows the current date without
prompt.
TIME:
Displays or sets the system time.

TIME [drive:] [/T | time] [/D]

  /D  Shows the selected clock device.
  /T  Outputs the current time without
prompt.
NLSFUNC:
Loads locale-specific information.

NLSFUNC [locale]
        [[drive:][path]filename]

  locale  Specifies a supported locale.

The locale info is loaded from a file
containing locale-specific information,
or the default COUNTRY.SYS if not
specified.
CHCP:
Displays or sets the character set.

CHCP [drive:][path][filename]

  filename  Represents a CPI character
            set file.

Type CHCP without a parameter to reset
to the default C64 ROM character set.
PROMPT:
Changes the MCS-DOS command prompt.

PROMPT [text]

  text  Specifies a new command prompt.

The prompt can be made up of normal
characters and the following special
codes:

  $B | (pipe)          $P Current drive
  $C : (colon)            and path
  $D Drive letter      $Q = (equal sign)
  $G > (greater-than)  $R Line break
  $H \ (backslash)     $S Space
  $I Drive identifier  $V Version number
  $N Drive number      $$ Dollar sign

Type PROMPT without parameters to reset
the prompt to the default setting.
MODE:
Configures system devices.

Device status:
  MODE [device]
Select charset:
  MODE CON[:] CP=yyy
Colors:
  MODE CON[:] COLOR=c1,c2,c3
Drive identification:
  MODE DRV[:] IDS=yyy
